chunks: And also what he narrated - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) who said:

I asked him about a man whom the month of Ramadan overtook while he was ill, and he died before recovering. He said: 'There is nothing upon him, but it is compensated on behalf of the one who recovers then dies before compensating.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who dies in Ramadan while still ill and has not made up missed fasts?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between the obligation of fasting (*wajib*) and its compensation (*qada*) in cases of death during illness. The Imam establishes that if one dies while still incapacitated, the duty is lifted entirely, whereas if recovery occurred but death preceded the makeup, the estate must provide compensation, reflecting the Shia principle that obligations persist until fulfilled or excused by death.
